{
  "title": "How should access to the 'provider' API be authenticated?",
  "body": "Given that the provider API is intended for use by cities (and their vendors/patners) and NOT the general public, how should providers implement access control on their API endpoints? \r\n\r\nSimple option would be for LADOT to issue a shared secret at the time when providers are granted an API.\r\n\r\nLonger term, probably need a more cryptographic or account-oriented solution, since cities may want the ability to authorize 3rd parties (e.g. vendors) to access MDS data on their behalf.",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": "2018-09-26T03:52:13Z",
  "updated_at": "2018-10-01T17:38:58Z"
}

    "body": "I’d argue that it might be a good choice to remove transport protocol completely from this spec, or at least put it into a separate optional spec. \r\n\r\nFor example, you could imagine a provider and agency agreeing that the provider just emails a large data dump of all trips every week or that the provider FTPs the data to a central server. Authentication would be figured out differently in each of those situations. ",
    "created_at": "2018-09-12T20:11:48Z",
    "updated_at": "2018-09-12T20:11:48Z"
  },

    "body": "@aickin that's an interesting thought, I can see how that kind of setup could be more useful to certain organizations that maybe aren't quite prepared to deal with API calls and AWS databases etc. \r\n\r\nThat being said... do we have any of those agencies listening in, that want to put forth their thoughts on this matter?     "id": 420806608,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/openmobilityfoundation/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-420806608",
    "body": "I would suggest a [JWT](https://jwt.io/) that is issued by the provider to LADOT (or other agencies). This provides a lot of customization from the provider's perspective if there is other information they want to encode in the token and allows the providers to authorize accounts with well-defined permissions for accessing only MDS resources.\r\n\r\nFrom the agency's perspective it is also relatively easy to issue new tokens and track token usage to prevent improper access or sharing. We also have envisioned agencies being able to generate their own tokens with bounded from this master token for use by their employees or vendors which seems like a win.\r\n\r\nAnother benefit here from the agency perspective is that each token can be issued only for their relevant area of operation (city or district) so there's no concern about any sort of improper access of data from areas outside the agency's purview.\r\n\r\nIf it's helpful would be happy to provide some example tokens and requests.",
    "created_at": "2018-09-12T21:37:55Z",
    "updated_at": "2018-09-12T21:43:53Z"
  },
